01 · Electro-permanent basics

Two stable states. One short pulse.

A hybrid magnet: a hard permanent magnet with constant polarity, plus a softer reversible magnet wrapped in a coil. A brief pulse through the coil flips the soft magnet. Then the electricity cuts off completely.

1 · Pulse ON→2 · Lift→3 · Power cut→4 · Lower→5 · Pulse OFF→6 · Lift + lower (plate stays)
OFF · demagnetized Power available

The magnetic flux circulates inside the module. Nothing is attracted: the magnet can be positioned and removed freely.

Power while holding0 W
1Low-carbon steel cores (poles)
2Static magnet: hard, typically Neodymium, constant polarity
3Reversible magnet: softer Alnico, polarity easily flipped
4Ferro-magnetic load
5Coil (electrical solenoid) around the Alnico magnet
Turning ON

A brief pulse through the coil flips the soft magnet so it aligns with the hard magnet. Their fields merge and grip the external steel.

Turning OFF

A reverse pulse flips the soft magnet the other way, cancelling the hard magnet's external field.

Zero static power

Once switched, the electricity cuts off completely. The EPM keeps its hold or release state with no ongoing power and no heat.

02 · What reduces the grip

Air gap, overhang, temperature.

Move the slider and watch the lifting force. Curves are taken from the Winkle training charts; values shown are read from those charts (≈).

≈ 50% force
at 1.0 mm

Minimal increases in air gap reduce the magnetic force on the material significantly. This reduction is not as pronounced with an electromagnet.

Paint, scale, oil, warped plates, snow and ice all create an air gap.

≈ 1,750mm overhang
10 mm plate

The overhang of material outside the magnet depends on the thickness of the material. This is comparable with electromagnets.

≈ 97% power
40 °C
Danger zone. Prolonged heat permanently damages the permanent magnets and the coil. Once compromised, lift capability is not recoverable.

High-temperature materials and prolonged exposure to heat cause permanent damage to the permanent magnets and coil inside the magnet.

Same lift. Very different power story.

Key advantages of the electro-permanent magnet

Energy efficient

Uses power only for a fraction of a second, during the switching transition.

Fail-safe

Relies on permanent magnets, not a continuous circuit: a power outage will not cause it to drop a lifted load.

No overheating

Standard electromagnets get hot under continuous current. EPMs stay cool.

FactorElectro-permanentElectromagnet
Power during holdZero: only uses power during switchingContinuous while active
Power lossMaintains holding force if power is lostDrops load if power is lost; a BBU is required to maintain power to the magnet
Coil duty cycleMinimal heat: power only during switchingMust be designed to specific duty cycles; more susceptible to heat damage
Air gap / safetySmall air gaps, typically 1 mm or less (.04 in)Able to lift through larger air gaps, standard 1/8 in (3 mm)
Flux field depthTypically a shallow fieldLarger depth of field
ApplicationAmbient to slightly elevated material temperaturesAmbient to hot product
AbuseNot susceptible to mechanical abuseCan handle more mechanical abuse

05 · Electro-permanent operation

Run a lift, stage by stage.

Use the control panel exactly as on the lifter: YELLOW is a safety interlock and never acts alone. Press YELLOW, then GREEN to magnetize or RED to demagnetize. Or press Guided cycle to watch the five stages.

Turn the Main switch ON.
Drag the view to rotate it.

Control panel

Main switch OFF

Power control · lifting power at First MAG

Magnet selection · which modules lift

GREEN = selected · RED = not selected

Crane

Magnet0 %
Plates held0
Heighton stack
Power ramp: 10 · 25 · 50 · 75 · 100 %
STAGE · 01

First MAG (pick-up)

Press YELLOW + GREEN. First shot: 2–6 s. Power steps: Level 1 = 10 %, Level 2 = 25 %, Level 3 = 50 %, Level 4 = 75 %. Final = 100 %.
STAGE · 02

Lift check · 200–300 mm

Hoist slowly. Check the load is balanced. Confirm only ONE plate is being picked: multiple plates means go to Stage 3. No cross/long travel yet.
STAGE · 03

Inching · only if > 1 plate

Press INCHING to soften the magnetic field slowly. Release when one plate remains. WARNING: a plate is expected to drop during inching. Keep 200–300 mm height, no people near the load.
STAGE · 04

Full MAG · 100 %

Press YELLOW + GREEN again, only while the plate is in the air. Auto: 30 s after First MAG, or 15 s after inching. Blinking yellow = automatic counter has started.
STAGE · 05

DEMAG (place & release)

Place the load. Slacken the chains. Press YELLOW + RED. Magnet releases. NEVER demagnetise a load that is still hanging in the air.

Magnet selector: pick which module(s) do the lift

GREEN lit = that module is selected for the lift; RED lit = not selected. Always confirm the selector pattern before MAG. Example lifter nameplate (fixed beam, horizontal). Click a row to select it in the simulator.

Pattern#LengthWidthCapacity

Permissible overhang (same nameplate)

Plate thickness → permissible overhang.

The power control dial sets the lifting power during First MAG. Once a full magnetization holds the load, the system stays at 100 %. The dial alone does not change magnetization: repeat the cycle.

07 · Customer conversations

Discover. Qualify. Compare. Validate.

Four steps from first call to a quote that comes back fast.

01

DISCOVER

Understand the application, parts to be lifted, process, issues the customer is having and their end goals.

02

QUALIFY

Confirm material, temperature, contact issues, crane capacity and all necessary information to qualify that an electro-permanent system will work for the application.

03

COMPARE

Compare and discuss pros and cons of electro-permanent vs electromagnet systems and their trade-offs.

04

VALIDATE

Validate and gather all information for crane, material to be lifted and electrical supply to reduce quote turnaround times.
